key_insight: Only constraints that remain closed after coarse-graining can be enforced exactly; for turbulence, linear constraints like incompressibility and global momentum survive filtering, while nonlinear PDE residuals can inject a wrong implicit closure.
engineering_relevance: For neural operators on coarse turbulent data, a simple Fourier-space projection can enforce physically valid constraints cheaply and improve long-horizon stability far more reliably than a full physics-informed residual.
method: Train a Fourier neural operator (FNO) on coarse turbulence fields.
Apply a closed-form O(N log N) projection to enforce continuity and global momentum exactly.
Optionally fit a constant subgrid flux to close the global energy balance on coarse data.
evidence_signal: On 2D isotropic turbulence, the projection reduced continuity error to 5.0e-7 and momentum-balance error to 8.6e-11, while increasing bounded 448-step rollouts from 0.18 to 0.87; on resolved Kolmogorov flow, test-time optimization was ~3300× more expensive than projection.
watch_item: The approach relies on identifying constraints that stay valid under filtering; enforcing unclosed nonlinear balances without modeling subgrid effects can hard-code an incorrect closure into the learned operator.
paper_title: Only Linear Constraints Survive Coarse-Graining: Evaluating Physics-Constrained Neural Operators on Stochastically Forced Turbulence
